record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For the minimality problem for positive realizations of strictly proper rational discrete-time SISO transfer functions G(z), what mathematical framework gives effective necessary and sufficient criteria for the minimal order of a positive realization? In particular, can one determine whether the invariant-cone approach can be extended beyond the third-order case, or whether an alternative formulation such as factorization of positive matrices is the right general instrument for solving minimality questions?

evidence.quote: First of all, it is not clear what kind of mathematical "instruments" should be used to effectively tackle this problem.

By contrast, such approach, has lead to the determination of necessary and sufficient conditions for the third order case only. A different formulation, such as the factorization approach proposed by Picci and van Schuppen in reference [30], can be a viable and promising possibility.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a strictly proper rational transfer function G(z) of a discrete-time single-input single-output (SISO) linear system. A positive realization of G(z) of order N is a triple (A, b, c) with A ∈ R^{N×N}, b ∈ R^{N×1}, c ∈ R^{1×N} whose entries are all nonnegative, such that G(z) = c (zI − A)^{-1} b. The minimal positive realization order N*(G) is the smallest N for which such a nonnegative triple exists; it can be strictly larger than the McMillan degree of G(z).

Two general lines of attack have been proposed:
(i) the invariant-cone (polyhedral cone) approach, in which one seeks a proper polyhedral cone K ⊂ R^N invariant under A and compatible with b and c, with minimality of N tied to the minimum number of extreme rays of such a K; and
(ii) the positive-matrix factorization approach, in which one studies factorizations H = U V of an associated nonnegative Hankel-type matrix H into nonnegative factors U, V, with N*(G) related to the nonnegative rank of H.

Problem. Provide a mathematical framework that yields effective necessary and sufficient criteria for the minimal order N*(G) of a positive realization of an arbitrary strictly proper rational SISO transfer function G(z). In particular:

(a) Determine whether the invariant-cone approach can be extended to give necessary and sufficient conditions for N*(G) beyond the third-order case (currently the only general order for which such conditions, expressed via invariant polyhedral cones, are known).

(b) Alternatively, decide whether a nonnegative factorization formulation (factorization of an associated nonnegative matrix into nonnegative factors) provides the correct general instrument, and if so, derive from it computable necessary and sufficient conditions characterizing N*(G) for transfer functions of arbitrary order.
artifact.category_tag: positive linear systems / minimal positive realizations
artifact.status_search_result: The general minimality problem for positive realizations of SISO rational transfer functions remains open. Necessary and sufficient conditions are known only in restricted settings — e.g., third-order transfer functions with distinct positive real poles, and certain classes with nonnegative or negative real poles or specific pole/residue structures. Recent works (e.g., on transfer functions with two distinct poles, 2022) continue to address special cases, indicating no general criterion has been established via either the invariant-cone method or nonnegative factorization.

status_evidence.title: Minimal Positive Realizations of Transfer Functions With Real Poles (IEEE)
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions for nth-order transfer functions with negative real poles to admit a positive realization of dimension n.
status_evidence.claim: Only restricted classes (specific pole structures) admit known necessary and sufficient conditions.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations for linear systems with two-different-pole transfer functions (2022)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies minimal positive realizations for transfer functions with two distinct poles.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to address only special pole configurations, indicating the general problem is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations of a class of third-order systems
status_evidence.snippet: Treats the third-order case via invariant-cone style arguments.
status_evidence.claim: The invariant-cone approach has yielded necessary and sufficient conditions only for the third-order case.
